title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Multipoint ligand–ligand contacts and extended helical packing can raise both glum and sensitization relative to a mononuclear analogue by locking one chiral conformation and organizing the chromophores.
explanation: Intramolecular π–π, CH/F, and CH/π contacts in Eu(hfa)3(pybox) complexes asymmetrically arrange the diketonates and give |glum| about 0.15–0.46 with quantum yields of 34–41% in CD3CN. Adding facam to pybox pushes 5D0→7F1 glum to about 0.8–1.0 by suppressing quasi-racemic conformers, albeit with sub-1% quantum yields. A helical [Eu(+/-tfc)3(dpbp)]n polymer raises solid-state sensitization from 14% to 53% and glum from 0.09 to 0.16 versus the mononuclear complex. Aggregation of Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] only nudges glum from +1.38 to +1.45.
scope: Heteroleptic Eu(III)/Tb(III) β-diketonate complexes with chiral pybox, facam, or bridging phosphine-oxide ligands, in solution or as coordination polymers.
conditions: Solution data are solvent- and concentration-specific (for example CD3CN or acetone-d6); the polymer comparison is solid state.
caveats: Ligand–ligand locking does not remove the brightness trade-off: some of the highest glum values still have quantum yields below 1%. Tb analogues of the hfa/pybox series stay weakly emissive because of back-transfer.
